name: Mock Up's
description:
A mock-up is a representation used to explore or communicate the appearance, arrangement or physical form of a proposed design. Mock-ups range from rough representations to highly realistic models, but unlike fully functional prototypes they often reproduce only selected aspects of the intended design.

They allow designers and stakeholders to encounter a proposal more concretely than they can through verbal description alone.
whenToUse: Use mock-ups when questions concern visual hierarchy, scale, spatial arrangement, physical form or presentation and full functionality is unnecessary.
steps: Identify what the mock-up needs to communicate or test.
Determine an appropriate scale and level of detail.
Select materials or software suited to those questions.
Construct the relevant visual or physical features.
Place the mock-up in an appropriate context where possible.
Gather feedback against the intended design goals.
Revise or increase fidelity only when required.
lookOutFor: High visual fidelity can cause people to assume that underlying decisions are final.
A mock-up may look convincing while leaving important interaction or technical questions unresolved.
Make clear which aspects are represented accurately and which are placeholders.

resources.citation: Hallgrimsson, B. (2012). *Prototyping and Modelmaking for Product Design*. Laurence King.
